Subject: ACME evaluation: MAP update and potential go-live delay

Diego,

Quick update from our side after the trial integration run this morning. The evaluation team hit a blocker with our sandbox network (timeout on the streaming socket) that caused a re-run of the full eval harness. That means the gating tests we expected to finish by May 10 will likely slip — current estimate is we need an additional 10 business days to complete full pass + quality checks.

Attached: ACME_MAP_v3.xlsx (updated timeline, changed test owners) and the failing test logs. We still want to move forward with Redwood but need to reset the target close date and update the MAP (specifically: infra tasks, access, and validation windows).

Two asks:
- Can Redwood commit to provisioning a secondary eval endpoint (short-lived) to parallelize the remaining runs?
- Can we schedule a quick alignment call tomorrow to re-baseline the MAP and confirm procurement milestones?

Thanks — apologies for the late notice,
Tom

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval_run_0502.log (text)

Tom — thanks for the heads up and the MAP. I pulled the team together and sketched a rapid mitigation path below.

Short answer: we can provision a secondary, isolated eval endpoint for the next 14 days and run the remaining test permutations in parallel. That will require 1) an engineering sign-off for burst capacity and 2) procurement confirmation to accept a short-term addendum for the extra infra usage.

Proposed immediate steps (owners & dates):
- Provision parallel sandbox (Redwood infra) — owner: marissa_cole — ETA: 2027-05-03 18:00 PT
- Re-run failing harness on parallel endpoint — owner: ACME test team (Tom) with Redwood support — ETA: 2027-05-06
- Update MAP (milestones + procurement windows) — owner: diego_fernandez — deliverable: updated MAP + action matrix by 2027-05-03 EOD
- Procurement sign-off on short-term infra addendum — owner: rishi_malhotra / ACME procurement — target: 2027-05-07

If we do the above, realistic close target becomes May 21 (was May 10). I will update the MAP and the risk register and share by EOD.

Can you confirm Tom that ACME can accept a target close of May 21 and that procurement will prioritize the addendum? If yes, I’ll loop in legal for a light DocuSign amendment and marissa will start provisioning.

Diego

Laura — looping you in with a short executive brief. ACME (strategic mid-market account) experienced a sandbox networking failure during a scheduled run which forced re-execution of the evaluation harness. We have a mitigation (provision an isolated parallel endpoint) that preserves validation fidelity, but it incurs short-term infra costs and pushes the realistic close target from May 10 to May 21.

Ask (two items):
1) Approval to provision a 14-day parallel sandbox and acceptance of the one-time infra increment (estimated incremental cost: $4,200) to be billed as an addendum against the ACME trial scope. This will allow parallel runs and reduce overall slip.
2) Approval to offer a one-time service credit (up to $6,000) if ACME confirms procurement cannot sign the addendum and we do a second rebaseline — this credit is a commercial concession to preserve the relationship and keep momentum.

Why approve: ACME is a priority target in our west region and the account team has already invested pre-sales hours. The concession is within the quarter-level discount tolerance and will likely unlock a committed Dedicated conversation if close proceeds as expected after the evaluation.

Attached: short exec brief with timeline, cost estimate and action matrix (exec_brief_acme_0503.pdf).

If you prefer, I can brief you live for 10 minutes — marissa can walk you through the tech details.

Thanks,
